title: What is the lowest point below sea level on Earth?
description: The video measures heights from the sea level line, so the lowest point is the one furthest below it and its height is negative. It names the deepest place in the Pacific Ocean and gives its height with the minus sign, and checks the sign against the picture.
teaching_notes: One idea: a place below sea level has a negative height, and the lowest place is the one furthest below the line. Watch for students who write the depth as a plain positive number and so put the place above the sea.

video_script.why: The child finds the lowest point with respect to sea level and gives its height as a negative number.
video_script.substitution: A sea level line at zero with an ocean trench drawn far below it, with its depth measured down from the line.
video_script.anchor: a sea level line at zero with a very low ocean trench drawn below it
video_script.payoff_line: The lowest point is furthest below sea level, so its height is negative.

final_answer.value: Jia in the Mariana Trench, Pacific Ocean; approximately -10994 m.
final_answer.spoken: the Jia in the Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean, at about minus ten thousand nine hundred and ninety four metres
